description: This 3D bar chart, from the paper "Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners: A Comprehensive Evaluation and Beyond," illustrates the accuracy of three large language models—Davinci-03, ChatGPT, and BARD—across four different types of logical reasoning tasks: Inductive, Deductive, Abductive, and Mix. The horizontal axis displays the model names (Davinci-03, ChatGPT, BARD) and the reasoning type categories (Inductive, Deductive, Abductive, Mix), arranged in a grouped format where each model has a set of bars corresponding to each reasoning type. The vertical axis represents Accuracy, scaled linearly from 0 to 0.6, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The height of each bar corresponds to the model's accuracy on that specific reasoning task, with the color gradient (blue to yellow) visually indicating the value, where higher bars are more yellow. The tallest bars, representing the highest accuracy, are for ChatGPT on the Deductive task (approximately 0.6) and for Davinci-03 on the Inductive task (approximately 0.55). The shortest bars, indicating the lowest accuracy, are for BARD on the Inductive task (approximately 0.2) and for ChatGPT on the Abductive task (approximately 0.3). The bars are not sorted by height, and no bars are visually emphasized with special formatting like shading or outlines.
